summary: Diloxanide (given as diloxanide furoate) is a luminal (contact) amoebicide used to eradicate Entamoeba histolytica cysts from the bowel lumen. It is the drug of choice for asymptomatic passers of amoebic cysts and is given after a tissue amoebicide (such as metronidazole, tinidazole or dehydroemetine) has cleared invasive disease, to prevent relapse and transmission. It is NOT FDA-approved (it is supplied in the UK and many other countries and via WHO programmes); this record is based on BNF/WHO and SmPC-type information rather than a US label. It is poorly absorbed, acting locally in the gut, and is generally very well tolerated, with flatulence the most common effect. The standard adult dose is diloxanide furoate 500 mg three times daily for 10 days; for children it is about 20 mg/kg/day in three divided doses for 10 days.
indications: Eradication of Entamoeba histolytica cysts in asymptomatic cyst passers (luminal amoebiasis)
Follow-on treatment after a tissue amoebicide (e.g. metronidazole/tinidazole) for invasive intestinal amoebiasis or amoebic liver abscess, to clear residual luminal cysts

moa: Diloxanide furoate is a luminal (contact) amoebicide. After oral administration the furoate ester is largely hydrolysed in the gut, and the bulk of the dose remains within the bowel lumen, where diloxanide is directly amoebicidal against the cysts and luminal trophozoites of Entamoeba histolytica. Although its precise molecular mechanism is not fully defined, it is thought to act like other dichloroacetamides by destroying the parasite within the intestinal contents and mucosa. Because it acts in the lumen and is poorly absorbed systemically, it clears the cyst-carrier state but is not effective against invasive (tissue) amoebiasis, which requires a tissue amoebicide.

monitor: Parasitological clearance (follow-up stool microscopy) where indicated

preg: There are limited data on diloxanide furoate in pregnancy; it is generally avoided in the first trimester and used later only if clearly necessary. Where treatment of cyst carriage is required in pregnancy, specialist advice should be sought.
lact: Data on diloxanide in breast milk are limited. Given its low systemic absorption it is likely to pose little risk, but it should be used with caution during breastfeeding.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is required; diloxanide furoate is minimally absorbed and acts locally within the gut lumen.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is required; the drug acts within the bowel lumen with little systemic absorption.

minor: No clinically significant drug interactions are well documented owing to minimal systemic absorption
interactions.food: May be taken with food to reduce flatulence
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction (unlike nitroimidazoles, no disulfiram-like reaction reported)
interactions.diagnostics: No significant effects on laboratory tests

monitoring: Clinical response and resolution of cyst passage
Follow-up stool microscopy to confirm parasitological cure where indicated
counsel: This medicine clears the cysts of the amoeba parasite from your bowel to stop it coming back and spreading
Take the full 10-day course, three times a day, even if you feel well
Wind (flatulence) is the most common, harmless side effect and may be eased by taking it with food
Wash hands carefully and practise good hygiene to avoid passing the infection to others
Provide a stool sample afterwards if asked, to confirm the parasite is cleared
Tell your doctor if you develop a rash or other allergic symptoms
pk: Acts locally in the gut over the treatment course
The absorbed fraction peaks within about 1 hour; most stays in the lumen
The small absorbed fraction is rapidly conjugated and excreted (short half-life)
Local amoebicidal effect over the 10-day course
Store at controlled room temperature, protect from moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; supplied in the UK and via WHO programmes - this record is from BNF/WHO/SmPC sources
Luminal amoebicide of choice for asymptomatic cyst passers and for clearing residual cysts after invasive disease
Always follow a tissue amoebicide (e.g. metronidazole/tinidazole) when treating invasive amoebiasis - not effective alone for invasive disease
Very well tolerated; flatulence is the main side effect
Minimal systemic absorption means few interactions and no dose change for renal/hepatic impairment
Standard adult course is 500 mg three times daily for 10 days
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it - do not take a double dose. Complete the full 10-day course.
overdose: Diloxanide furoate has a wide margin of safety and overdose is unlikely to cause serious harm because little is absorbed. Manage any overdose supportively with symptomatic treatment of gastrointestinal effects; there is no specific antidote.
